name: Kampala Art Biennale
funding: Produced by Kampala Arts Trust and Afriart Gallery. KAB20 (2020) was co-funded by the EU and Pro Helvetia. TotalEnergies Foundation backed the 2018 mentoring programme; no later TotalEnergies money found.
watch: Founded in 2014 by Daudi Karungi. No edition since the virtual KAB20 in 2020; the site is now an archive.
records_note: Publishes no annual reports or accounts; its Partners page names the KAB20 co-funders, and the producing Kampala Arts Trust names its seven trustees.

name: Katuaq Greenland Cultural Centre
funding: About 33.6k cinema visits in 2023. Funded by Greenland's Self-Government and Kommuneqarfik Sermersooq (2M DKK each extra in 2026), plus GrønlandsBANKEN and Air Greenland.
watch: A self-owning foundation; its board is appointed by the Self-Government, the municipality, Visit Greenland and EPI. Bank (not under campaign) and state airline as sponsors.
records_note: Annual management reports 2018 to 2023 give results without full accounts; two unlabelled undated sponsor logos; the board is named in the 2023 report.

name: Kër Thiossane
funding: Tiny association (active through 2024); project grants from Langlois Foundation (2001), EU ACP Cultures (2010-12), UNESCO IFCD and the Francophonie.
watch: Media-art and digital-commons space in Sicap Liberté, founded 2002. Runs the Afropixel festival, a fablab and a garden.
records_note: Its website ker-thiossane.org refused the connection, so nothing could be checked; the Partcours festival page lists festival supporters only.

name: Kettle's Yard
funding: University of Cambridge gallery. Arts Council England, Research England, Cambridge City Council; corporate supporters include David Zwirner, Emmanuel College, Murray Edwards College, City Asset and Resolute AV.
watch: Retains Jim Ede's founding vision of intimate, unbranded domestic galleries.
records_note: Annual reports 2009-10 to 2024-25 are online with a 2024/25 supporters list; parent University of Cambridge publishes accounts; a committee is listed.

name: Kingston Creative
funding: Inter-American Development Bank (US$1.3M over three years), Bank of Jamaica, Digicel Foundation, Barita, Gore, National Bakery, PwC, the Clara Lionel Foundation and the Miami Foundation.
watch: Runs the Kingston Art District and Artwalk Festival; 118 murals painted. First Caribbean NGO to win a UNESCO-Aschberg grant, July 2026.
records_note: Posts annual reports 2021 to 2025, with financial statements in the 2023 report, a donor list and a board page.

name: Kröller-Müller Museum
funding: The Ministry of OCW, VriendenLoterij and the Helene Kröller-Müller Fonds are named in the site footer.
watch: Autonomous national museum inside De Hoge Veluwe national park.
records_note: The museum posts annual reports with accounts for 2017 to 2025, names its supervisory board, and names its main funders in the 2025 report.

name: Kunsthalle Basel
funding: Canton Basel-Stadt CHF 950k a year for 2024-27 (32% of budget); third-party grants about CHF 660k (30%); restaurant and property rent 22%; members 8%.
watch: In November 2023 an SVP member of the cantonal parliament demanded subsidy be cut over director Almusibli's ceasefire letters; the canton did not act.
records_note: It posts annual reports 2014 to 2025 with financial statements, names members and corporate supporters in the 2025 report, and lists its association board.

name: Kunsthalle Mannheim
funding: City of Mannheim, Hans-Werner and Josephine Hector (€50M for the Hector building) and their foundations, the Förderkreis, and a Stifterkreis of 57 persons, foundations and firms.
records_note: No annual report or accounts; support pages name the Hector family and foundations, and the Stifterkreis page lists the foundation council and executive board, undated.

name: Kunsthalle Recklinghausen
funding: Museen der Stadt Recklinghausen, NRW culture ministry, Kunststiftung NRW, Sparkasse Vest, Ruhrfestspiele (city and DGB union federation), Förderverein für Bildende Kunst; WDR 3 media partner.
records_note: A city museum with no report or board of its own; the city posts audited accounts, and the site shows four undated funder logos.

name: Kunsthalle Wien
funding: City of Vienna (MA 7) core funding. Sponsors: Dorotheum, Ottakringer, Vöslauer, Winzerhof Dockner, Das Teppich Werk, Ton & Bild. 2026 programme support from Institut français and the Mondriaan Fund.
records_note: Shows funders and sponsors as logos under 2026 headings; it posts no annual report, accounts or board list.

name: Kunsthaus Hamburg
funding: Hamburg's Behörde für Kultur und Medien supports it; the Claussen-Simon-Stiftung backed the Whispers show. Part of Kunstmeile Hamburg.
watch: Municipal exhibition hall for contemporary art. The Kemmler Foundation named earlier is on none of the pages opened.
records_note: A non-profit gGmbH that posts no annual report, accounts or board; the home page credits the Hamburg culture authority and Kunstmeile Hamburg by logo.

name: L'Appartement 22
funding: Founded by curator Abdellah Karroum. Supported through non-commercial international research grants, Prince Claus Fund, and independent publishing sales.
watch: Founded in 2002 as Morocco's first independent space for contemporary visual art and curatorial research. It is also a radio station (R22) and a residency for Maghrebi and African artists.
